_comment: Apple Watch lineup, 2026-09-04. The catalog held one watch (Series 6) against fourteen iPhones, so a hiker on any current model had nothing to pick. Every figure is Apple's own CASE weight from its Tech Specs page — the same support.apple.com source the Series 6 row uses — and every one was read twice, from support.apple.com AND from the matching apple.com/.../specs/ page, which agreed exactly on all fourteen. CASE ONLY, NO BAND: that is what Apple publishes and what the Series 6 row already stores, so a band has to be added as its own row — Apple does not publish band weights, so none are here. Two things that look like errors and are not: Apple's ALUMINIUM cellular case is lighter than the GPS one (37.8 g vs 36.9 g at 46mm, and the same inversion on Series 10), and the black Ultra 2 and black Ultra 3 weigh the same 61.8 g while their natural finishes differ (61.4 g vs 61.6 g) — the Ultras are stored as ONE row each on the natural finish, with the black figure kept in the quote, because a 0.2-0.4 g finish difference is below what a pack weight notices and catalog:audit rightly flags colour in a variant. Titanium ships cellular-only with a single published weight, so those variants carry no GPS/Cellular split. Older generations (Series 10, SE 2, Ultra 1) are not here — a follow-up if wanted. The Ultra rows carry the natural finish's figure and name the black one in the quote; the coating difference is a fraction of a gram, below anything a pack weight notices, and catalog:audit rightly flags a colour in a variant. That reasoning lives here rather than in the quote because the audit parses gram figures OUT of the quote to check them against the stored weight — a stray '0.2 g' of commentary in there is read as the citation and fails.

rows.name: Watch Ultra 3
rows.quote: Weight (natural): 61.6 grams; weight (black): 61.8 grams — 49mm Grade 5 titanium case (Apple Watch Ultra 3 Tech Specs). Stored as the natural finish.

rows.name: Watch Ultra 2
rows.quote: Weight (natural): 61.4 grams; weight (black): 61.8 grams — 49mm Grade 5 titanium case (Apple Watch Ultra 2 Tech Specs). Stored as the natural finish.
